scope: Parent integration review after blind factual audit. Not a new independent rating and not a revision to primary votes.

disagreements.annotation: Both plans repair premium pricing and fit their final capacity tables. Judges differ on buffer and scope; no new established numerical error in this disagreement.

The final main tables agree, but raw has an incorrect course comparison and a transition that can exceed the hard hour cap before termination notices expire. The broad Gemini math endorsement misses these qualifications. Grounded revises the draft five-client premium option in a labelled fallback; that is not necessarily an absolute constraint violation.

A pricing illustration and year-end staffing timing need qualification. Two months from October19 leaves some December availability, so no revenue this year is too definite. Preference also depends on how much weight to give unused van capacity.

Both reject the unaffordable plan and provide funded schedules. Gradual scaling, inventory reserve and margin assumptions receive different weight; no consensus is warranted merely because both say no.
Conservative initial spend competes with efficient use of the fixed agency fee and the deadline. Both arithmetic paths check out; risk tolerance explains the disagreement.

Referral rewards require room in the growth budget even if paid from gross profit. The grounded ramp also needs a continuing referral reserve. Budget completeness is a substantive qualification, not a reason to rewrite either vote.

Raw misdescribes its annual discount, while grounded membership projections assume unstated acquisition deterioration. Annual billing and sustained engagement are distinct outcomes. Different weighting is defensible.
Both select the same business. Tax framing and data safeguards compete with explicit time allocation and profit-based continuation criteria. No established contradiction in this preference split.
Commercial sequencing competes with product and inactive-pilot diagnosis. An arbitrary sales target is a proposed decision rule, not an observed fact. Neither ranking is a factual correction.
Both retain employment; employer conflicts and fallback options create the difference. These are useful scenario considerations, not source-fidelity requirements.

One answer negotiates the commitment while the other answers the offered binary more directly. This is a constraint-interpretation difference, conditional on whether remaining in the present role is available.
Both allocations total36000 and the payback arithmetic is conditional on80percent margin. The main difference is reserving evidence-gated spending and addressing launch/onboarding.

Both improve recruiting rather than cash alone. Pipeline ownership and measurement detail favor grounded for one judge; runway specificity and revisiting declined candidates favor raw. Founder-time wording remains ambiguous.

Flexible compensation and a measurable sourcing target compete with a stronger categorical pipeline diagnosis. Given missing burn and hiring-budget data, compensation assumptions cannot be conclusively validated.
Both select the domain-informed product. Held-out technical validation and procurement are central. Judges differ on distribution options and realistic paid-pilot timing.
Commercial specificity competes with early feasibility work. Neither answer fully validates data quality and sales timing; tie versus raw preference is a qualitative judgment.
